evidence.quote: The ingots with nominal composition of Fe39Co33Ni18Ti10 (at%) were prepared by arc-melting furnace under a protective argon atmosphere, using raw materials with high purity (Fe: 99.99%, Co: 99.95%, Ni: 99.995%, Ti: 99.999%). The ingots were turned over and melted five times to ensure homogeneity.
Then, the as-cast ingots were homogenized at 1273 K for 8 h in a quartz tube with argon atmosphere, and quenched into water.
Subsequently, these solution-treated ingots were isothermally aged at 873 K with different time, and quenched into water. The isothermal aging time is 10 min for A10-CCA

evidence.quote: The ingots with nominal composition of Fe39Co33Ni18Ti10 (at%) were prepared by arc-melting furnace under a protective argon atmosphere, using raw materials with high purity (Fe: 99.99%, Co: 99.95%, Ni: 99.995%, Ti: 99.999%). The ingots were turned over and melted five times to ensure homogeneity.
Then, the as-cast ingots were homogenized at 1273 K for 8 h in a quartz tube with argon atmosphere, and quenched into water.

Subsequently, these solution-treated ingots were isothermally aged at 873 K with different time, and quenched into water. The isothermal aging time is 10 min for A10-CCA, 30 min for A30-CCA, 60 min for A60-CCA and 120 min for A120-CCA.

The scanning electron microscope-backscattered electron (SEM-BSE) image (Figure 1a) and inset electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) phase map revealed that A10-CCA exhibited a duplex phase structure comprising an FCC matrix (dark-gray contrast in the BSE)
and body-centered cubic (BCC) islands (bright-gray contrast in the BSE image).
The dark-field TEM image shown in Figure 1c highlights the L12 nanoprecipitates, which had an average particle size of approximately 5 nm and a number density of ≈1.9×1015 m−2.
When the isothermal aging time was extended to 30 min, the L12 nanoprecipitates grew to an average particle size of approximately 10 nm (Figure S4, Supporting Information).
